messages:
sasha: Quick q — cluster-autoscaler is scaling up our gpu-nodepool in eu-west-1 fine but scale-down often doesn't happen. Nodes stay at 1 pod each, cost is spiking. Anyone tuned this recently?

kevin: Can you paste the CA deployment args and an example of one of those pods (resources/annotations)?

sasha: here's the CA args from our helm values (redacted):
```
--expander=least-waste
--balance-similar-node-groups
--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m
--scale-down-unready-time=10m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
--max-node-provision-time=10m
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=true
```
The pods are fairly small (0.25 GPU) but many are GPU-bound so they land on separate nodes.

miguel: least-waste is often bad for GPU packing. It tries to minimize leftover capacity and will spin up the smallest node for an incoming pod, but it doesn't do cross-node binpacking well for fractional-GPU requests. For GPU pools I usually switch to `--expander=most-pods` or use balanced node-groups + binpack-friendly instance sizes so CA can pack multiple pods per node.

jen: Agreed. Also tune scale-down timings and thresholds. We had better results with:
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=8m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.35
--scale-down-unready-time=15m
```
Lowering unneeded-time helps when jobs finish quickly. But watch flapping.

rana: Two extra gotchas we've hit: 1) daemonsets (gpu-device-plugin, monitoring) can make nodes look "used" — set `--ignore-daemonsets-utilization=true`. 2) pods without `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true` will block evictions. For batch workloads add that annotation and a lower priorityclass so CA can evict them first.

kevin: Also check `skip-nodes-with-local-storage`. We had it true and CA refused to remove nodes with local tmp dirs even though pods were gone. For our GPU worker pools we turned it to false because we don't use local-ssd for critical data.

miguel: If you're using spot/interruptible instances, prefer an on-demand fallback node group with slightly higher priority. We implemented a small mapping in our provisioning config so CA prefers spot groups but will fall back when capacity is exhausted. That plus `--balance-similar-node-groups` helped even out fragmentation across AZs.

ops-bot: [autoscaler] ScaleDown: node-group gpu-eu-west-a reduced from 4 -> 2 (reason: underutilized) at 2026-03-01T15:12:34Z

sasha: Nice. Anyone have a short checklist I can run through? Want to avoid adding churn.

jen: Checklist (quick):
- switch expander to `most-pods` and test for 24h
- set `--ignore-daemonsets-utilization=true`
- lower `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 8-10m temporarily
- set `--scale-down-utilization-threshold` to ~0.35
- ensure GPU pods have `safe-to-evict` annotation or run with preemption-friendly priorityclass
- check `skip-nodes-with-local-storage` and set to false if safe
- enable `--balance-similar-node-groups` if you have multi-AZ node groups
- monitor for flapping and spike in pod evictions

rana: One more: update nodegroup sizes and instance types to allow denser packing. E.g., move from lots of small 1-GPU instances to mixed 4-GPU instances for workloads that can share. CA packs better and reduces per-GPU overhead.

kevin: I'll submit a small helm values patch to change expander + flags and set a 24h feature-window. Sasha — want me to apply it to a canary namespace first?

sasha: Yes please. Canary on eu-west-1/gpu-canary and we'll watch cost + PodPending/PodEvicted metrics. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:
